Before deciding to retire, it’s wise to examine a broad set of personal, financial, and lifestyle factors so that you can make a smooth transition and enjoy a comfortable, sustainable retirement. Below is a practical checklist to guide your decision‑making.

| Category | Key Questions & Considerations |
|----------|--------------------------------|
| **Financial Readiness** | • **Savings & investments** – Do your 401(k), IRA, and other retirement accounts provide enough income to cover projected expenses? <br>• **Cash flow** – Have you calculated a realistic monthly budget that includes housing, food, transportation, entertainment, and contingencies? <br>• **Debt** – Have you paid off or significantly reduced high‑interest debt? <br>• **Inflation protection** – Are your investments diversified to hedge against rising prices (e.g., inflation‑indexed bonds, real estate, dividend‑paying stocks)? <br>• **Longevity risk** – Will you outlive your savings? Consider annuities, systematic withdrawals, or a “safe withdrawal rate” strategy. <br>• **Tax strategy** – How will withdrawals impact your tax bracket? Consider Roth conversions or strategic withdrawals. |
| **Health & Insurance** | • **Health status** – Are you in good health or managing chronic conditions? <br>• **Medicare eligibility** – At 65 you can enroll, but do you need supplemental (Medigap) or Medicare Advantage plans? <br>• **Long‑term care** – Do you have long‑term care insurance or a plan to pay for potential nursing home or home‑care expenses? <br>• **Vision & dental** – These costs often rise with age; ensure coverage. |
| **Lifestyle & Purpose** | • **Daily routine** – What will you do every day? Will you have hobbies, volunteer work, or part‑time employment? <br>• **Social network** – Do you have a supportive community or will you need to build new connections? <br>• **Travel & leisure goals** – How much will you travel or pursue costly hobbies? <br>• **Spouse or partner** – Coordinate retirement dates and plans; align on shared goals. |
| **Location & Housing** | • **Cost of living** – Compare your current location to potential retirement destinations. <br>• **Housing needs** – Will you downsize, stay put, or relocate? Consider maintenance costs, property taxes, and climate suitability. <br>• **Proximity to healthcare & family** – Accessibility to medical facilities and loved ones can be important. |
| **Social Security & Pensions** | • **Optimal claim age** – Determine the best time to start receiving Social Security (full retirement age, delayed benefits, or early benefits with a trade‑off). <br>• **Pension rules** – Understand any vested benefits, early‑retirement penalties, or survivor options. |
| **Estate & Legal Planning** | • **Will & Trust** – Ensure a current will, consider a living trust for asset protection and ease of transfer. <br>• **Power of Attorney & Health Care Proxy** – Designate trusted individuals to make decisions if you become incapacitated. <br>• **Beneficiary designations** – Update beneficiaries on IRAs, life insurance, and other accounts. |
| **Tax Implications** | • **State taxes** – Some states tax Social Security and retirement income; consider relocation to a lower‑tax state. <br>• **Required Minimum Distributions (RMDs)** – Know when RMDs start and how they affect your tax bracket. |
| **Contingencies & Flexibility** | • **Emergency fund** – Maintain 6–12 months of living expenses in a liquid account. <br>• **Plan for unexpected expenses** – Consider how you’ll handle sudden health events, market downturns, or significant home repairs. <br>• **Re‑employment options** – If needed, keep a part‑time job or consulting role in mind. |
| **Emotional & Psychological Readiness** | • **Identity shift** – Reflect on how you’ll adjust from a working identity to a retiree lifestyle. <br>• **Mental health** – Stay proactive about mental wellbeing; consider clubs, groups, or counseling if needed. |

### Steps to Take

1. **Run a detailed retirement budget** – Include fixed and variable costs, with a 3–5% inflation buffer
